Tuesday, January 29, 1963 FEDERAL REGISTER 819
Executive Order 11079
PROVIDING FOR THE PRESCRIBING OF REGULATIONS UNDER WHICH  
MEMBERS OF THE ARMED FORCES AND OTHERS MAY ACCEPT  
FELLOWSHIPS, SCHOLARSHIPS, OR GRANTS
By virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 2603 of Title 10,  
United States Code, I hereby designate the Secretary of Defense, with  
respect to members of the Army, Navy, Air Force, and Marine Corps,  
the Secretary of the Treasury, with respect to members of the Coast  
Guard when it is not operating as a service in the Navy, and the  
Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare, with respect to com-,  
missioned officers of the Public Health Service, to prescribe regulations  
under which members of the Armed Forces and commissioned officers  
of the Public Health Service may accept fellowships, scholarships, or  
grants from corporations, funds, foundations, or educational institu­
tions organized and operated primarily for scientific, literary, or edu­
cational purposes. To the extent practicable, such regulations shall be  
uniform.
J ohn  F. K ennedy
T he  W hite  H ouse,
January 25,1963.
[FR. Doc. 63-r999;  Filed, Jan. 25,1963; 3 :00 p.m.]

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The designation continues as amended. EO 11382 section 13 (signed 1967-11-28; no separate effective-date clause) replaced the Secretary of the Treasury with the Secretary of Transportation; EO 12608 section 15 (signed 1987-09-09, no effective-date clause) replaced the Department and Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare with the Department and Secretary of Health and Human Services in the listed orders including 11079; EO 13286 section 69 replaced the Secretary of Transportation with the Secretary of Homeland Security effective 2003-03-01 (section 92 of EO 13286: "This order shall become effective on March 1, 2003."). The held current-law note extract prints the designation with the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Secretary of Health and Human Services.

research_rationale:
EO 11079 (28 FR 819, signed 1963-01-25; held official Federal Register text, page location high) is a single designation made under section 2603 of title 10, United States Code: the Secretary of Defense (Army, Navy, Air Force and Marine Corps members), the Secretary of the Treasury (Coast Guard when not operating as a service in the Navy) and the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare (commissioned officers of the Public Health Service) are to prescribe regulations under which members may accept fellowships, scholarships or grants, uniform so far as practicable. The held original has no sunset, expiry, condition or revocation. Three later orders changed the officers named: EO 11382 section 13 (1967-11-28; Treasury to Transportation), EO 12608 section 15 (1987-09-09; Health, Education, and Welfare to Health and Human Services) and EO 13286 section 69 (effective 2003-03-01; Transportation to Homeland Security). None revokes or supersedes the order. The held current-law extract of the Code (only the extracted note text is held, so it is corroboration and not a claim source) prints the order as amended by all three as a note to 10 U.S.C. 2603, so the authority section named in the order is still in the Code, and the note carries no ending statement. The ofr_catalog search reports three hits for this order, which are the three amendments. Cutoff limit: the held Code edition is current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 are not reflected.

The packet's chain also labels one amendment as EO 12977, but the held text under that label (a source-ladder file named for EO 12977) is EO 13286 section 69; the official text of EO 12977 does not mention EO 11079, so EO 12977 is not recorded as an event.","independent_command_check":"The order is one command (designation to prescribe regulations) naming three designees for three groups of persons; the three designations cannot end separately on the held evidence, and each continues with its current officer.","savings_check":"See savings reason; no savings text exists, and regulations issued by the designees rest on the designation and do not make it exhausted.","scope_check":"Each amendment substitutes an officer's title in the single designation; none changes what the designees are to do. Tuesday, January 29, 1963 FEDERAL REGISTER 819
Executive Order 11079
PROVIDING FOR THE PRESCRIBING OF REGULATIONS UNDER WHICH  
MEMBERS OF THE ARMED FORCES AND OTHERS MAY ACCEPT  
FELLOWSHIPS, SCHOLARSHIPS, OR GRANTS
By virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 2603 of Title 10,  
United States Code, I hereby designate the Secretary of Defense, with  
respect to members of the Army, Navy, Air Force, and Marine Corps,  
the Secretary of the Treasury, with respect to members of the Coast  
Guard when it is not operating as a service in the Navy, and the  
Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare, with respect to com-,  
missioned officers of the Public Health Service, to prescribe regulations  
under which members of the Armed Forces and commissioned officers  
of the Public Health Service may accept fellowships, scholarships, or  
grants from corporations, funds, foundations, or educational institu­
tions organized and operated primarily for scientific, literary, or edu­
cational purposes. To the extent practicable, such regulations shall be  
uniform.
J ohn  F. K ennedy
T he  W hite  H ouse,
January 25,1963.
[FR. Doc. 63-r999;  Filed, Jan. 25,1963; 3 :00 p.m.]
